tools-tech.dwp_take: Companies are now planning to spend a fifth of their IT budgets on AI by 2027, yet over half of IT leaders expect to miss their ROI targets on these investments. This matters because digital workplace teams will be caught between pressure to deploy AI solutions and the reality that most won't pay off as promised, forcing difficult conversations about what actually stays versus what gets cut. After three decades in this space, I've seen plenty of shiny tech spending cycles, but expecting positive returns within a year while simultaneously missing targets is a new flavor of optimism I haven't encountered before.

digital-culture.title: How Dropbox plans to prevent AI brain rot in its workers
digital-culture.excerpt: Concerned about its workers losing brainpower as they outsource work to artificial intelligence, Dropbox is considering using cognitive training tools, like memory exercises and attention-span trainin
digital-culture.dwp_take: Dropbox is worried their employees will turn into digital zombies if AI does all their thinking, so they're rolling out memory games and attention exercises plus analog retreats where executives breathe and stare at trees. This matters because every company wrestling with AI adoption is quietly panicking about the same thing: if we automate everything, do our workers actually atrophy? Here's my take after three decades in this space: if your retention strategy hinges on cognitive training apps and mandatory unplugging, you've probably already lost the plot on what actually keeps people engaged at work.

digital-culture.dwp_take: Some writer at Fast Company decided to extract financial advice from horror movie villains like Ghostface and Samara, because apparently regular financial experts weren't spicy enough. This matters to workplace communicators because it's a textbook example of how to bury useful information under so much creative framing that your actual audience gives up halfway through. Look, I've been doing this thirty years and I'm telling you: if your message needs Jason Voorhees to make people listen, your message probably isn't that strong to begin with.
